english_transcript:
Doctor: Yes, come in and sit down. What problem are you having?

Patient: Namaste, doctor. My name is Anish. I am 25 years old, and I have been having a cough for more than three weeks. I took medicine from the pharmacy, but it did not help.

Doctor: Do you bring up any phlegm with the cough?

Patient: Yes, I do. It is yellow in color. I also noticed small streaks of blood twice.

Doctor: Do you get fever?

Patient: Yes, doctor. In the evening, when I check with a thermometer, it shows 99. At night I sweat a lot; my clothes get completely wet.

Doctor: Have you had any weight loss?

Patient: Yes, doctor. I checked yesterday, and my weight has reduced by about 5–6 kg. I also do not feel hungry at all.

Doctor: Over how many months did you lose 5–6 kg?

Patient: Over about six to seven months. I have been checking every month, and now I can see that I have lost about 5–6 kg.

Doctor: Do you feel short of breath?

Patient: Yes, a little. When I walk, I feel breathless.

Doctor: Did you have breathlessness earlier too?

Patient: No, earlier I was completely fine.

Doctor: Do you smoke or use anything like beedi or cigarettes?

Patient: Yes, I have been smoking beedis daily for the last 10–12 years. I smoke around 10 beedis a day.

Doctor: Does anyone at home have this kind of problem?

Patient: My elder brother had TB about six years ago.

Doctor: Did he take treatment for TB?

Patient: Yes, he completed the full treatment, and he recovered. He is healthy now.

Doctor: What work do you do?

Patient: I am a laborer, doctor. My work involves dust and soil.

Doctor: Do you have any other old illness, like diabetes or blood pressure problems?

Patient: No, doctor. By God's grace, everything else is fine.

Doctor: Okay. I will need to listen to your chest. Take a breath. On the upper right side, the air entry is reduced, and there are some added sounds. It looks like TB is a possibility, so we will need to do some tests first.

Patient: Doctor, TB is a very serious disease, isn't it? I have heard that.

Doctor: No, do not worry. With medicines, it can get better, and the government also provides free medicines. But you must take them regularly.

Patient: Okay.

Doctor: I will write some tests for you: sputum AFB, sputum culture, and CBNAAT.

Patient: Thank you, doctor.

Doctor: Yes, that is all.
